We uncover the important characteristics of an RNN-based solution with experimentation on a lab-scale Canal Lock CPS emulator with live validations and attack scenarios. For the first time, we demonstrate actual, real-time use of a RNN-based model as a DT for performing live analysis on an operational CPS. Based on the observed results, we highlight the importance of a DT model's training interval, prediction interval and CPS polling interval in the process of anomaly detection. We uncover the limitations in anomaly detection due to real-time synchronization needs of the RNN-based DT. We highlight this uncovered tug of war between synchronization and anomaly detection is inherent in any complex CPS that is monitored and synchronized by relying on the same sensor streams of ground truth for both synchronization as well as anomaly detection.

articleTitle: A Personalized Privacy Protection Data Uploading Scheme for Mobile Crowdsensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Mobile crowdsensing is a typical application of the Industrial Internet of hings and brings a promising opportunity to construct powerful industrial systems and services. The existing privacy protection schemes usually adopt a unified privacy protection policy for all sensing data due to lack of effective privacy metrics, thereby resulting in excessive or insufficient protection of privacy information and low accuracy of sensing data. To tackle these issues, in this paper, we propose a personalized privacy protection data uploading (PPDU) scheme based on game theory and sensing user's historical spatio-temporal data. In PPDU, a personalized privacy measurement algorithm is designed to obtain the personalized privacy degree of user sensing data. Based on the privacy degree, a user uploading behavior game is designed by employing an incomplete information game, and a game-based spatio-temporal sensing data uploading method is proposed for user privacy protection. Simulation experiments with real trajectory data show that the PPDU scheme makes a reasonable balance between retaining high quality of crowdsensing service and protecting user's privacy.

Author Keywords: Mobile crowdsensing, personalized privacy protection, game theory, privacy degree, industrial Internet of Things

articleTitle: Image Threshold Segmentation Based on Auxiliary Individual Oriented Crossover Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Image threshold segmentation based on entropy is classical method. The time cost of applying the two-dimensional maximum entropy and enumeration threshold segmentation method is unacceptable, so that the genetic algorithms is adopted to improve efficiency. Because of the premature convergence of traditional genetic algorithm, the performance of image threshold segmentation is constrained. We propose a 2-D maximum entropy threshold segmentation method based on the auxiliary individual oriented crossover genetic algorithm (AIOXGA) to improve the speed and success rate of image threshold segmentation. The introduction of the AIOX operator reduces the blindness of the genetic algorithm and improves the optimization efficiency. This method was compared with enumeration method, standard genetic algorithm and original oriented genetic algorithm(OGA) in image segmentation experiments. The results show that the performance of this method is better than that of traditional methods.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Authentication Schemes Against Clone Node and Sybil Attacks in Wireless Industrial Internet
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Security is becoming an increasingly important factor for any of today's wireless communications systems. For mission-critical wireless industrial networks, a new and increased level of significance is urgently required. Various cyber-attacks, such as a clone attack and sybil attack, seriously threaten industrial network security. Therefore, we propose a strategy utilizing identity and channel state information to detect clone attack and sybil attacks. Firstly, we collect identity to make a preliminary assessment between the two types of attacks. Secondly, the physical layer authentication approach is adopted to undertake attack detection, utilizing the channel state information differences between the legitimate and malicious nodes. We verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach through simulation and attack experiments.

Author Keywords: Physical layer authentication, industrial wireless communication, channel state information, channel impulse response

articleTitle: A Speculative Parallel Optimization Method for Industrial Big Data Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Apache Spark is one of the most advanced distributed computing platforms at present, more and more industrial big data algorithms are implemented on this platform to achieve better performance. However, some of the algorithms cannot be executed on Apache Spark in parallel because of their complex inner control dependencies. In order to solve the problem, by introducing Software Thread-Level Speculation technique, this paper proposes a method to optimize industrial big data algorithms, and makes them run on Apache Spark in parallel. Specifically, the proposed method analyzes how complex inner dependencies affect algorithm's parallelism, then speculatively partitions the algorithm into subtasks to conquer these dependencies, and predicts inputs for the subtasks. After executing the subtasks in parallel, the results are collected and validated, the correct results are kept and committed while the incorrect ones are abandoned. By this way the optimal parallelism for industrial big data algorithms can be achieved. The experiments show that by the proposed method, the particle swarm optimization algorithm can achieve speedup by 150%-230% comparing with the unspeculative one. Therefore, the execution efficiency of low parallelized algorithm on Apache Spark can be markedly enhanced by the proposed optimization method.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Wireless Augmented Reality on Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) technologies provide a novel experience for users to interact with the real-world environment by integrating virtual content into real circumstances. However, wireless AR applications have trouble to ensure visual security in complex and various scenarios. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning based wireless AR, which adaptively revises the location of the virtual content to avoid obscuring real-world context. The AR devices adaptively make display strategies according to the partially observable Markov decision procession (POMDP). We incorporate mobile edge computing (MEC) to release the computing pressure and assist wireless AR device to make decisions. Finally, we compare the proposed algorithm to ε-greedy algorithm, which is widely used in reinforcement learning problems. The experiment results show that the proposed algorithm learns faster and shows better performance of avoiding obstructions. Besides, we discuss the assistance of MEC to improve the performance of learning convergence. Experiment results show that the assistance of MEC brings the advantage of efficient learning.

articleTitle: QoE Control for Dynamic Adaptive Video Streaming Over HTTP at Access Point
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: Recent research shows that when multiple dynamic adaptive streaming over HTTP (DASH) clients stream Internet videos simultaneously via a wireless access point (AP), they may experience poor quality of experience (QoE). This is because DASH clients in a wireless local area network (WLAN) independently estimate current available bandwidth and make bitrate selections. Lacking coordination in the WLAN causes competition for downlink bandwidth, introducing unnecessary bandwidth fluctuations especially when some clients start streaming. Such bandwidth fluctuations lead to cascading video bitrate changes on each stream, resulting in dramatic video quality variations, in the worst case, for example, video stalls. To address this problem, it is essential to mitigate the bandwidth competition by coordinating DASH clients in the WLAN. In this paper, we propose a QoE control framework at the AP to dynamically allocate bandwidth for each DASH client based on their real-time streaming performance feedback. To deal with uncertainty in Internet traffic besides streaming traffic, we design robust control algorithms to minimize stalls while balancing bandwidth sharing among clients. We implement and evaluate our solution with real systems under various settings. Extensive evaluation results show that our design significantly reduces average video stalling duration by 57.1% and improves the average video bitrate by 42.0% for all clients when compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

Author Keywords: Dynamic Adaptive Video Streaming over HTTP

articleTitle: Agent Communications in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Internet (ICII)
abstract: The use of edge computing techniques can be extremely beneficial to distributed applications when is it more efficient to process data in proximity to data sources than to transmit data to remote computational resources. The introduction of edge computing has created a number of communication challenges beyond what is typically experienced in the traditional client-server model. While the area of edge computing is in its infancy, few existing implementations address the wide-range of issues related to multi-protocol discovery, identity, messaging, security, and stateful operation of agents operating across heterogeneous computational and network architectures.
